fixture_name: NE Edmonton Ring Road planning-stage RSA — Canada TAC planning (real sample, Alberta Transportation 2009)
subject: judge-baseline

justifications.substance: Interchange-spacing deficiency and mainline weaving at a system/service interface is a substantive Stage 1 safety issue with credible rear-end/sideswipe mechanisms and network-level congestion propagation recorded in the audit's own observations.
justifications.evidence_grounding: EV-CA-039 verbatim quote directly supports the pivotal spacing/functional-area claim (1970 m, 1670 m vs 3000 m) and EV-CA-003 grounds the off-limit consequence propagation, with assumptions traced to recorded inputs.
justifications.jurisdiction_correctness: Correctly treats sub-preferred spacing as a safety_concern rather than a compliance breach (normative_basis_note null), keeping the categorical distinction intact and framing remedies at the planning-stage functional plan level.
justifications.recommendation_quality: Specific and actionable dual remedy (adopt 3000 m spacing in next functional-plan iteration, or collector-distributor roadways clearing the weaving sections) plus verification against 2041 staging-year weave volumes; viable at planning stage though relocation cost is unstated.
justifications.vru_coverage: Explicitly acknowledges the ring-road mainline is fully access-controlled with no pedestrians or cyclists, scoping road users to vehicle occupants; VRU impacts are not applicable here and are duly acknowledged.

justifications.substance: The finding identifies a real process gap with direct road-safety consequences: twice-flagged local-access-in-system-interchange conflicts remain undispositioned in the finalised functional-plan record, so neither the safety issue nor the accept/reject decision is closed out.
justifications.evidence_grounding: The pivotal claim (mandatory response report with accept/conditionally-accept/reject options) is supported by the verbatim EV-CA-038 quote, and EV-CA-003 supplies verbatim text for the fully-and-consistently-documented duty, with EV-CA-006 anchoring the Planning Stage = Stage 1 context.
justifications.jurisdiction_correctness: Correctly scoped as a compliance_question under the Alberta Stage 1 instrument, citing §5.6.2 response-report semantics without conflating the documentation duty with a new safety judgment about the access connections themselves.
justifications.recommendation_quality: Specific and actionable: issue and file the §5.6.2 response report dispositioning each audit issue with reasons, showing removal of the local access connections or documented justification for retention before plan finalisation.
justifications.vru_coverage: VRUs are not applicable on the fully access-controlled mainline, and this is explicitly acknowledged with the reasonable extension note that the flagged connections route traffic toward the local cross-road network where VRUs travel.
